children: The abrupt resignation of OP Bhatt, Chairman of the Board of Coforge Ltd, and the subsequent resignation of DK Singh, Chairman of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC), has raised some fundamental questions on the process and approach to the annual Board evaluation procedure adopted by companies.

From available press reports, it has emerged that the internal audit carried out on the Board evaluation process found that some parts of the evaluation reports were made available only to Bhatt and Singh and were not shared with other Board members. It has also been reported that the Chairman of the Board secured a low rating, which was also not shared with the NRC and the Board.

The remit of this piece is limited to the efficiency and the rigour attached to the Board evaluation procedure and does not seek to draw conclusions on what exactly went wrong and who is responsible for the same. Lessons from Coforge have to be digested and necessary corrections made in the larger context of good corporate governance.

Most companies undertake this exercise with the seriousness as mandated by the regulators. The coverage extends to evaluation of each Board member, the Board as a whole and the Chairman of the Board. The onus of this exercise is with the Chairman of NRC with the support of external agency.

title: Decoding Coforge saga
